subject.title: Feature request: fallback model chain for compaction and LCM summaryModel

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` contract now, and should Lossless `summaryModel` fallback live in the Lossless plugin or in a generic context-engine SDK seam?
rationale: This is not a strict bug fix: it adds a new config/default surface, changes provider/auth routing during compaction, and crosses from core embedded compaction into plugin-owned Lossless/context-engine behavior.

options.title: Approve Embedded Core Fallback Plus Plugin-Owned Lossless
options.body: Add an explicit embedded compaction fallback chain in core and keep Lossless `summaryModel` fallback in the Lossless plugin unless a missing SDK seam is proven.

options.title: Design One Context-Engine Fallback Contract
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers choose a shared API for embedded compaction, Lossless, and other context-engine summaries.

options.title: Keep Summary Fallbacks Outside Core
options.body: Decline the new core config key and direct operators to provider routing, compaction providers, or external/plugin-owned fallback handling.

recommendation.title: Approve Embedded Core Fallback Plus Plugin-Owned Lossless
recommendation.body: Add an explicit embedded compaction fallback chain in core and keep Lossless `summaryModel` fallback in the Lossless plugin unless a missing SDK seam is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related PR review already framed the valid feature and the required decision boundaries for replacement semantics, compaction-owner coverage, and LCM handling.
